reasoning_summary: 0001: Framing only (reader wants an unconditional answer); no mathematical content to check, harmless. 0002: Blank. 0003: Two claims. (a) DNF-SAT is in L — TRUE: a DNF formula is satisfiable iff some term contains no complementary pair of literals, and scanning terms while comparing literal pairs with a constant number of O(log n) pointers is a logspace decision procedure; the phrase 'satisfy the first disjunct' is loose (the first term may be self-contradictory, e.g. x AND NOT x, so one must find the first CONSISTENT term), but the corrected reading is the standard argument and the claim DNF-SAT in L holds. (b) 'if it is NP-complete then L=NP' — valid under logspace many-one reductions, since L is closed under logspace reductions, so NP reducible to a language in L gives NP subset of L, hence L=NP; under the default Karp (poly-time) notion it would only yield P=NP, so the step is justified only in the logspace-reduction setting that steps 0005 and 0007 make explicit. Accepted as justified in context, with that qualifier implicit. 0004: Blank. 0005: Main claim TRUE: if L=NP then for any A in NP we have A in L, and a logspace transducer can decide A and output a fixed satisfiable DNF string (e.g. 'x') on acceptance and a fixed unsatisfiable/ill-formed string (e.g. 'x AND NOT x') on rejection, so A reduces in logspace to DNF-SAT; this uses that DNF-SAT is nontrivial (it has both yes- and no-instances), which it is. The parenthetical generalization 'every problem in NP is NP-complete under logspace reductions' is, strictly, false for the two trivial languages: nothing nonempty many-one reduces to the empty set and nothing but Sigma* reduces to Sigma*, so those two remain non-complete even if L=NP. This aside is a standard over-generalization, is not used anywhere in the chain (only the DNF-SAT instance is needed), and does not affect the conclusion; flagged as an imprecision, not a failure of the argument. 0006: Blank. 0007: 'L=NP iff DNF-SAT is NP-complete under logspace reductions' — the forward direction is 0005 and the reverse is 0003(b); both directions established, so the biconditional is justified. 0008: Blank. 0009: (i) 'no unconditional statement is currently available' — justified: by 0007 an unconditional proof that DNF-SAT is not logspace-NP-complete would prove L != NP, an open problem. (ii) 'P != NP need not be assumed' — justified: L is contained in P, so P != NP implies L != NP, i.e. L != NP is the strictly weaker assumption. (iii) 'L != NP is the weakest hypothesis guaranteeing the result' — justified by the equivalence in 0007: the target statement is logically equivalent to L != NP, so any sufficient hypothesis must imply it. The one soft spot is that 0009 drops the 'under logspace reductions' qualifier, and under plain Karp reductions the corresponding weakest hypothesis would be P != NP rather than L != NP; read in the logspace setting fixed by 0005 and 0007, the step is correct. Overall: every load-bearing step is justified; the only defects are the loose phrase 'the first disjunct' in 0003, the false-for-trivial-languages parenthetical in 0005, and the dropped reduction qualifier in 0009, none of which breaks the chain to the stated conclusion. Verdict VALID.
